The relationship between vehicle SOC and AC power drawn by the EVSE was found using the vehicle characterization tests outlined above, and the results are shown in Figure 10. Hyundai Ioniq 5 and Bosch charge curve The example shown above is a good representation of what was observed throughout low-power DC vehicle characterization. Relatively constant power around the EVSE’s maximum is drawn for most of the SOC range until you get above 90%, where the rate will start to slow down as the vehicle battery approaches full charge. This is due to the relatively low power in comparison to the vehicle’s optimal charging power. This effort captures the effect that the vehicle’s battery management system has on the charging load, like the small drop in charging rate after the 90% SOC point that occurs in every Hyundai Ioniq characterization test that was performed, in addition to the charging ramp-down rate. The charge acceptance curve generated in this section is then implemented in the CHIL to model the power draw of all the EVSE and vehicle combinations. 18 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 4 Simulating Control Capabilities Expanding electrification with flexible charging loads and installing on-site DER for energy generation and storage presents an opportunity for load management systems to optimize site operations to reduce energy and infrastructure costs. This optimization is possible with communication and control systems that monitor and coordinate DER assets and flexible charging loads with grid and site operations. The complex nature of these objective functions requires a simulation environment to rapidly test and troubleshoot control capabilities prior to lab demonstrations and field deployments. The following simulation results highlight the capabilities of each control to support site planning and cost-benefit analysis. 4.1 Simulation Results The site controllers presented in Section 2.3 were developed and tested within a simulation environment that resembled the experimental test bed, except that all objects and interactions were simulated.
